conditions: Serial execution; no local task tests, agents or other profilers ran concurrently.
Private user/network/PID namespaces and fresh configuration for every sample; no forced GC or profiler.
Dependency lock, automatic feature behavior, observer and exact Host are matched across Package variants.
Kernel page caches, CPU frequency and ambient machine activity were not controlled; two samples per variant/profile.
Ledger seed creation is outside the measured Host scope; resumed cold replay is included.
measurementBoundary: CPU and charged-memory counters cover the Host cgroup, including Workers and reaped children, through final observation before shutdown.
Observer, tmux, synthetic HTTP server and preparatory Ledger seed process are outside that cgroup.
Final RSS sums live process smaps_rollup readings; it is not aggregate peak process-tree RSS.
I/O counters belong to final surviving processes and omit exited children; they are not total process-tree I/O.
Charged-memory peak includes non-RSS charges and is not a cumulative allocation counter.
These runs do not measure allocations, GC, scheduler wakeups or largest main-thread tasks.
All individual gate breaches are retained, including the candidate background autocomplete-setup failure.

conditions: Exact certified Pi 0.85.0 binary and existing current-revision verifiers for both Package variants; no runtime source changes during the batch.
Fresh private HOME/XDG configuration per run and isolated user/network/PID namespaces; no overlapping Host workloads or other profilers. Ambient machine activity and kernel page caches uncontrolled.
GC logging enabled on the native Host and inherited Workers; no forced collection or CPU profiler. Diagnostic overhead is included in these totals, not ordinary liveness acceptance.
CPU sums waited native Host phases; maximum sampled RSS is the maximum across sequential phases, not their summed peaks. Reader, tmux/Expect and sibling HTTP fixtures excluded.
RPC/PTY verifiers deliberately terminate Hosts by SIGTERM or HUP after assertions; raw native signal exits are retained separately from successful verifier exit.
Web uses exact synthetic fetch responses and mount-private hosts/NSS files in its own network namespace; SSRF validation remains enabled. No live service, credentials or provider network.
measurementLimits: RSS sums sequential per-process smaps_rollup readings, nominally 20 ms apart plus scan time. These are sampled sums, not an instantaneous continuous peak or a proved lower bound on that peak. Short-lived unseen processes and process-read races are reported.
Last and tail-one-second median RSS are sampled end-of-run observations, not proof of a steady-state plateau. Linux wait maxRSS is not peak process-tree RSS.

Allocation values are conservative lower bounds only for complete unambiguous GC log cycles, with a one-byte rounding margin per cycle. Differing capture coverage, native allocations, uncollected tails and child logs prevent a total-allocation reduction claim.
GC pause sums include all accepted p fields, may combine VMs/Workers and are not CPU time or one uninterrupted main-thread pause. Observed maxima do not bound unseen pauses.

Parent /proc I/O maxima include kernel-accounted reaped descendants where available; child counters are not added again. Still-unreaped or unavailable descendant I/O can be absent. Block operations are not bytes; context switches are not wakeups.
Feature-specific offline verifiers complement full automatic Naming/Usage observers; they do not alone certify those automatic features or every external service.

conditions: Same fixed Pi 0.85.0, 120x40 terminal, two actual children per run, private fresh profiles, user/network/PID namespaces and GC logging for both variants. Cold Ledger contains 24 executions with 800000-character results.

All eight verifiers completed both child Tools, checked birth-bound reaping and automatic Naming request/persistence plus Usage refresh once. Background workloads persisted two outcomes and observed the parent while children ran.

The existing cgroup CPU/memory boundary includes native Host, Workers and descendants. The external sampler starts before Pi outside that cgroup; observer, tmux, HTTP fixtures and Ledger seeding remain outside.

A private first Extension records starts of 10-ms main-thread timer callbacks in memory and writes once on shutdown. It adds diagnostic callbacks/allocations; no production observer or Package source was changed.
Separate 75-second diagnostic observation budget; no responsiveness gate passed to these runs. Raw visible-feedback maxima remain recorded, without certification.
measurementLimits: Same sampled-RSS, partial-I/O and complete-GC-cycle limits as recoveryResourceComparison. Host stderr covers parent and its Workers, not complete child GC logs; whole-tree CPU/RSS still includes children.

For a non-yielding main-thread task wholly between two recorded callback starts, that callback interval is an upper bound on its elapsed duration. It also includes idle time, GC, scheduler wait and probe cost; it is not an exact JavaScript-task duration.

Coverage begins at probe evaluation and ends at its shutdown callback, excluding earlier Host startup and later teardown. Phase labels describe the preceding callback and can straddle an event boundary; exact interval timestamps are retained.
Startup extension-loading intervals are included separately, not hidden by reporting only active-Agent intervals. Two samples per variant cannot establish the absence of rare stalls.

conditions: Six serial native observations, no warmups or discarded workload samples; direct foreground, cold-Ledger Code Mode foreground and background, twice each in mirrored order.

Both real children completed and were reaped in every run; automatic Naming request/persistence and Usage refresh each occurred once. All owned scopes were unloaded, inactive and dead.

The first collector stopped after a valid native capture because its whole-worktree provenance included the known report-only diff. Validation was corrected to allow exactly those five documentation files, then the same saved capture was validated and the remaining five runs continued. No native sample was replaced.

All six capture the same report-only source diff; production Package and observer Source are unchanged at e43. Two passes per workload are finite acceptance evidence, not proof that rare events can never occur.
